original_question: For every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, is the degree deg(f) bounded above by a polynomial in the sensitivity sens[f], where sens[f] = max_x |{i in [n] : f(x) != f(x^i)}|?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open problem "Sensitivity versus Block Sensitivity": "For any f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} it holds that deg(f) <= poly(sens[f]), where sens[f] is the (maximum) sensitivity, max_x |{i in [n] : f(x) != f(x^{\oplus i})}|."
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual statement. It has the correct domain and codomain f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, the correct complexity measure deg(f), the correct use of maximum sensitivity sens[f], and the correct polynomial-relation form "deg(f) bounded above by a polynomial in sens[f]." It also targets the degree formulation that the paper explicitly lists, not just the more common block-sensitivity version.
missing_details: The paper leaves deg(f) implicit via standard Analysis of Boolean Functions notation; to make the question stand-alone, deg(f) should be specified as the degree of the unique multilinear real polynomial representing f on {-1,1}^n, not degree over F_2.
Your notation x^i should be defined explicitly as the input obtained from x by flipping its i-th coordinate; the paper writes this as x^{\oplus i}.

The quantifiers hidden in "bounded above by a polynomial" should be made explicit: there should exist a single universal polynomial p such that for every n and every Boolean function f, deg(f) <= p(sens[f]).
It should be explicit that there are no extra assumptions on f such as monotonicity, symmetry, balance, or low degree; the statement ranges over all Boolean functions on {-1,1}^n.

If you want the formulation to be paper-faithful in context, note that the paper immediately remarks that the more usual equivalent formulation is bs[f] <= poly(sens[f]), where bs[f] is block sensitivity.
refined_question: Does there exist a universal polynomial p such that, for every integer n >= 1 and every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, the degree deg(f) of the unique multilinear real polynomial agreeing with f on {-1,1}^n satisfies deg(f) <= p(s(f)), where s(f) = max_{x in {-1,1}^n} |{i in [n] : f(x) != f(x^{\oplus i})}| and x^{\oplus i} denotes x with its i-th coordinate flipped?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation noted in the paper: does there exist a universal polynomial p such that, for every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1}, one has bs(f) <= p(s(f)), where bs(f) is the maximum, over inputs x, of the number of pairwise disjoint coordinate sets B_1, ..., B_k subseteq [n] such that flipping all coordinates in any one block B_j changes the value of f at x?
justification: This draft is targeting the paper's unnumbered problem "Sensitivity versus Block Sensitivity" on PDF page 2, not a numbered conjecture/theorem: arXiv:1204.6447 is a symposium list of open problems, and it does not contain Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3. The paper's statement matches your draft almost verbatim. The only nearby paper-specific refinement is the first remark right below it, which says the more usual statement is bs[f] <= poly(sens[f]) and that this is equivalent because bs[f] and deg(f) are polynomially related. Since the front matter says notation and definitions are taken from standard Analysis of Boolean Functions conventions, the main work needed to make your draft fully stand-alone is to spell out the meaning of deg(f), the bit-flip operation, and the universal quantifier hidden in poly(sens[f]).
